sites.rationale: L15 and L16 both explicitly state 'N-terminal Twin-Strep affinity purification tag and SNAP-tag', and L15 demonstrates functional cAMP responses (GloSensor assay) to two agonists in a stable clonal cell line, confirming both surface trafficking and receptor function are preserved. The N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0) is the only extracellular terminus on ADRB2, which lacks a signal peptide (residues 1–33 extracellular, TM1 at 34–58). The tag is >33 residues from TM1. A clonal HEK293G cell line stably overexpressing full-length human β2AR with an N-terminal Twin-Strep affinity purification tag and SNAP-tag (TS-SNAP-β2AR) was used in GloSensor luminescence assays. Both L15 and L16 explicitly state the tags are N-terminal. ADRB2 has no endogenous signal peptide, so the tag prepends before M1.

sources.claim: Figure 2 shows the time courses of GloSensor TM luminescence responses stimulated by increasing concentrations of isoprenaline (Fig. 2a ) and salbutamol (Fig. 2b ) in a clonal HEK293G cell line overexpressing the human β 2 -adrenoceptor containing an N-terminal Twin-Strep affinity purification tag and an N-terminal SNAP-tag (TS-SNAP-β 2 AR 37 ).
All receptor constructs were N-terminally FLAG tagged.

Four DNA insert fragments were also purchased from Twist Bioscience (South San Francisco, CA, USA), which comprised nucleotide sequences encoding the human β 2 AR with an N-terminal HiBiT tag (connected by a linker consisting of the following amino acid sequence: GSSGGSSGGS) and several mutations within the β 2 AR sequence, namely either a double mutation of the asparagine residues Asn6 and Asn15 to alanine residues (Ala) (HiBiT-β 2 AR_N6A_N15A fragment) or a triple mutation including the same two N-terminal asparagine residues in addition to another asparagine residue Asn187

literature_notes: All three ledger-supported surface tag sites converge on the same junction (N-terminal prepend, insert_after_residue=0) because ADRB2 is a GPCR with no endogenous signal peptide and a single extracellular N-terminus (residues 1–33). They are reported as three separate sites because they represent independent experimental validations with distinct tag modalities (FLAG, SNAP-tag, HiBiT) and different validation levels. L1 and L5 further corroborate the N-terminal FLAG and HiBiT sites respectively with detailed construct architectures. L12 and L13 mention HA-tagged β2AR but do not state the tag position explicitly and cannot independently pin a junction; they are consistent with the N-terminal prepend but do not add a new site. L14 mentions SNAP-tagged β2AR without stating position; L15/L16 are used instead. ECL1 (96–107), ECL2 (172–197), and ECL3 (296–306) are extracellular loops but no ledger line reports a tolerated insertion in any of these loops for ADRB2; they are not proposed. The C-terminal intracellular tail (residues 328–413) is not a surface site.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP fusion (stop codon removed, AscI/PacI cloning) places the fluorescent protein at the intracellular C-terminus (topology: residues 328–413 intracellular); not a surface tag site.

β2AR::GFP truncated at R328 failed to traffic to the plasma membrane and localized perinuclearly (likely ER retention), demonstrating that the intact C-terminal tail beyond R328 is required for surface trafficking.
